summary: Existence-only search (scripts/z52d_p2_NC0_exist.c; every S-line of a 13,200-sample re-verified exactly; every last failure re-checked with the full counter z52b_fingerprint_count) over ALL primes p<=1e7 for m=5..48: last failures m=7..19 unchanged from the <=1e5 list (2,241,19,181,37,12241,281,353,20521,83449,2081,35281,353); beyond 1e5 the tail moves a lot: 20/p 90001->2763601, 24/p 97777->620929, 28/p->1532161, 32/p->3991681, 36/p->8763841, 44/p->7559641, 48/p->9961249 (5/p, 6/p: no failure to 1e7). Prime-only failures lie in (m^2,2m^2) for every m=20..48 (e.g. m=20: 401,421,503,601,641,761), consistent with Pomerance-Weingartner arXiv:2511.16817 (m>=20 numerics). A 10-term OEIS search for the prefix returned no hit.
not_done: Did not verify PW's theorem; did not check whether the complete last-failure list (not just the last element) matches PW's tables; 1e7 is a lower bound only (last failures for m>=36 sit within 0.4-1% of the window top, so they are censored).
next: Push the window for m=36..48 (last failures censored near 1e7) to 1e8 with the existence counter (about 20 s per 1e7 for all m, so ~5 min) and reread PW's tables.

summary: Computed Vmin(p) (least v in 4Z∪(8Z-p), v>=3, with a divisor d≡-1 mod v of p+v) for all 108,283 primes p≡1 (4), p<=3e6, v<=160: records 3(5),4(17),7(97),8(457),23(1009),87(2521),116(3361) exactly as the repo records. Independence model with empirical per-shift failure frequencies q_v(size bin, p mod 8): expected #{p<=3e6: Vmin>V} = 14.4 (V=23), 3.1 (V=31), 0.36 (V=47), 0.006 (V=116) versus observed 166, 69, 16, 0. So the premise 'independence predicts unbounded Vmin' is wrong (the model predicts a finite, rapidly decaying tail; E#{Vmin>116}≈0.006), but the model under-predicts the mid-range tail 10-50x: failures across shifts are positively correlated.
not_done: Did not fit the single-shift constants C_v from EXSET_SHIFT_DIVISORS §2 (used empirical q_v instead); did not decompose the excess by (p mod 3, mod 5) or p-1 smoothness; Vmin beyond 3e6 not computed.
next: Condition the Vmin tail on p mod 3,5,7 (and smooth p-1) and check whether the 10-50x excess disappears, as the joint-census analysis of EXSET_SHIFT_DIVISORS §6.3 suggests.

summary: Exact avoidance search over all primes p<=1e7 (existence with q∤xyz, scripts/z52d_p2_NC0_exist.c mode 1): no solution with 3∤xyz fails only at p=3 and p=241; 'no 5' fails only at 5, 'no 7' only at 7; 'no 4', 'no 8', 'no 9' never fail. 4/241 has exactly 8 unordered solutions, all containing a multiple of 3 (exact check). But 3-adic unit-solvability is not obstructed: for p mod 81 every unit residue class is reached by some unit triple (241 ≡ 79 mod 81 is in the solvable set), so the 3-adic obstruction hypothesis is not supported; the exception looks global and sporadic.
not_done: No proof of why 241 fails; the 3-adic check is a residue-level heuristic (mod 3^k, k<=81), not a Z_3 local-solvability proof. Composite n with no-3 failure were not separately characterised beyond n ≡ 0 mod 3 (trivial).
next: Test whether 4/241's eight solutions are explained by a global reason (e.g. Mordell–Schinzel / a quadratic-form genus obstruction over Q(sqrt(-3)) ) and whether 241 is the only prime with no unit-denominator solution mod 3-adic and mod 2-adic data together.

summary: Proth primes k·2^n+1 (k odd ≤15, p≤1e7; 38 primes, 30 of them ≤1e5) vs U(p)/log²p: median 0.56 for the 30 small ones against 1.07 for all p≡1 (4) in (1e3,1e5]; against controls matched on p mod 840 at the same size (≤1e5) the ratio is 0.54, and matched on (p mod 105, v2(p-1)) it is 0.71. Against random controls in [5e6,1e7] the naive ratio is 0.40 but that is a size artefact. The deficit persists after 2-adic matching, so it is not only v2(p-1); interpret cautiously (n=30).
not_done: Did not test the size confound beyond 1e5 (only 3 Proth primes in [1e6,1e7]); did not run an O(sqrt p)-per-x U-counter, so no Proth primes above 1e7; did not compare the odd part k of p-1 at fixed size.
next: Compare U/log²p for primes with p-1 = k·2^n·(smooth) against p-1 with a large odd prime factor, at fixed size ≤1e6, residue-matched mod 840.

summary: Per family (16 repo families, p≡1 (4), p∈(5e4,1e5]): among the 10 families with an exception ≤1e5, Spearman(CV, last exception) = +0.86 (p=0.002), i.e. the high-dispersion families have later last exceptions, which is the direction the item predicts; but Spearman(mean, last) = −0.94 (p=5e-5), so mean and CV are confounded across these 10 points and the item's 'dispersion, not mean' claim is not separated. Families with mean 19–32 and no exception at all (x|y, z≤n²) show the mean alone does not decide.
